title: CompAct-Bench: A Benchmark for Working-Context Compaction in Long-Horizon Agent Tasks
trick: Cut a solved agent run at 25/50/75%, have twelve models squeeze the history to 10% of its characters, let the same executor finish on the same action budget: success drops from 100% to 57% average.
framing_stripped: Called 'a 200-task process-level benchmark' for 'working-context compaction' with 'Iterative Ratio Calibration (IRC)' that makes compaction 'measurable as an execution-critical model capability'; it is 200 trajectories the executor solved three times out of three (79 BrowseComp, 96 SWE-bench Verified, 25 internal CompanyBench), each cut once at one of three points, a summary of the pre-cut history written by one of twelve API models under a shared 'Please summarize the above history concisely' prompt and edited by repeated calls until it is 10% of the body's character count, then three fresh continuations by a fixed executor (Claude Opus 4.8; GPT-5.5 Codex on CompanyBench) under the reference run's remaining action count, scored strict Avg@3 (sec. 2-3, App. A-B); plus an environment-only control (no history, no summary) on Coding and Search (App. F) and a six-label error annotation by GPT-5.6-Sol over failed continuations only (App. G).
method_equations: Reference trajectory for task $t$ (eq. 1): $$\tau = (a_1, o_1, \ldots, a_{T-1}, o_{T-1}, a_T),$$ where $a_i$ is the $i$-th executor action, $o_i$ the tool or environment observation that follows it, and $a_T$ the terminal action; $T$ is the action count. Boundary $b < T$ with $b = \lfloor sT \rfloor$, $s \in \{0.25, 0.50, 0.75\}$, one $s$ per trajectory, assigned stratified by benchmark and length tertile (App. C.3). Pre-boundary history (eq. 2): $H_b = (a_1, o_1, \ldots, a_b, o_b)$; the system prompt and task instruction are a 'retained head' carried verbatim and excluded from $H_b$ and from the ratio (App. A.2). Compaction (eq. 3): $M_b = C_\phi(H_b; r)$, where $C_\phi$ is the evaluated model with its prompt and $r$ the target retention ratio; realised ratio (eq. 4): $r_{\mathrm{actual}} = \ell(M_b) / \ell(H_b)$ with $\ell(\cdot)$ character length. Main setting $r = 0.10$ (sec. 2.2). IRC (App. B): for a candidate $M$, $\rho(M) = \ell(M)/\ell(H_b)$ and relative error $e(M) = |\rho(M) - r| / r$ (eq. 7); stop when $e(M) < \epsilon$ or after $K$ compactor calls. Stage 1 (shrink): from ratio $\rho_{i-1}$ request $\widetilde{\rho}_i = \max(\alpha \rho_{i-1}, \beta r)$ (eq. 8), $\alpha < 1$ the contraction, $\beta < 1$ the allowed overshoot. Stage 2 (anneal): with $M^\star$ the closest candidate so far, gap $g_i = r\,\ell(H_b) - \ell(M^\star)$ (eq. 9) and edit size $s_i = \max\!\left(1, \lfloor \min(|g_i|/2,\; 0.4\,\ell(M^\star))\, \gamma^{i-1} \rfloor\right)$ (eq. 10), $\gamma < 1$ the decay; $g_i > 0$ restores omitted material, $g_i < 0$ removes retained material; 'The full history and incumbent are both supplied, and the compactor is asked to edit the incumbent rather than rewrite it from scratch' (App. B.2). Hyperparameters: $r = 0.10$, $\epsilon = 0.03$, $K = 30$, $\alpha = 0.82$, $\beta = 0.90$, $\gamma = 0.85$; acceptance interval $[0.097, 0.103]$ (App. B.4). Continuation: executor receives the retained head, $M_b$ as 'Preloaded assistant context' and a harness-specific resume instruction (Table 7), restarts from the environment state at $b$ rebuilt by replaying the first $b$ tool calls (App. F.2), with at most $T - b$ new actions; 'Compaction itself is not subtracted from this executor-action budget' (App. A.4). Score (eq. 5-6): $\mathrm{Acc}(C_\phi) = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}|} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{D}} y_i$ over instance set $\mathcal{D}$, with per instance $\mathrm{Avg@3}_i = \frac{1}{3} \sum_{j=1}^{3} y_{ij}$, $y_{ij} = 1$ when continuation $j$ of instance $i$ ends within $T - b$ actions in a terminal state the source evaluator accepts (strict success); other endings are 'budget exhaustion' (all $T - b$ used) or 'early failure'. Headline (Table 2, strict Avg@3 %, 200 instances, $r = 0.10$): Claude Opus 5 68.5 (Search 62.0 / Coding 81.2 / Workspace 40.0), Gemini 3.8 Flash 65.5 (57.0 / 75.0 / 56.0), Kimi K3 62.0, GPT-5.6-Sol 59.5 (51.9 / 76.0 / 20.0), DeepSeek V4 Pro 57.8, HY3 57.5, GLM 5.3 Flash 57.0, Qwen 3.8 Flash 54.5, GLM 5.2 52.0, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview 51.5, Qwen 3.7 Plus 48.5, Doubao Seed 2.1 Pro 46.0; mean 56.7; bootstrap 95% CIs over tasks, Overall top vs bottom [62.0, 74.5] vs [40.0, 52.5] (Table 12). Stage (Table 13, means over compactors): Search 52.9 / 42.6 / 34.6 at 25 / 50 / 75%, Coding 64.0 / 72.7 / 86.1, Workspace non-monotonic peaking at 50%; 'nine of the twelve compactors show a monotonic decrease on Search, whereas ten show a monotonic increase on Coding' (sec. 3.3). Compaction input $H_b$ (Table 11, tokens): Search 8.2K to 29.3K, Coding 2.3K to 5.5K, Workspace 41.2K to 90.0K; within-domain prefix length vs accuracy $|\rho| \le 0.03$ (App. G.4). Environment-only control (Table 14): Coding without $H_b$ from boundary state 66.7 / 58.1 / 71.9 vs from initial state 48.5 / 35.5 / 15.6; with $M_b$ (mean of 12) 64.0 / 72.7 / 86.1, gain $-2.7$ / $+14.6$ / $+14.2$; Search without $H_b$ 26.9 / 15.4 / 7.4 vs with $M_b$ 52.9 / 42.6 / 34.6, gain $+26.0$ / $+27.2$ / $+27.2$. Coding pre-boundary edit indicator: 86.9% with an edit vs 53.0% without (Mann-Whitney $p = 3 \times 10^{-8}$) (App. F.3). Failure composition (App. E.4): 91.6% / 92.0% / 97.7% of failed Search / Coding / Workspace continuations exhausted the budget; successful continuations used median 55% / 86% / 93% of the source remainder. Ratio adherence (Table 9): 2,400 compactions, median realised ratio 0.0986, 86.0% within $[0.097, 0.103]$ (Coding 93.6%, Search 86.9%, Workspace 59.7%; Doubao 52.5%); mean IRC calls per instance 4.6 (Kimi K3) to 11.8 (Claude Opus 5). Error labels (App. G, failed continuations only, Table 16): critical omission 47.8% of early failures / 48.8% of budget exhaustions, factual distortion 40.3 / 35.2, premature commitment 56.7 / 46.0, lost resolution 0.0 / 3.6, progress/state loss 55.2 / 44.6, constraint/goal distortion 25.4 / 24.3, any 92.5 / 85.8; unit judgments 69.1% preserved, 25.3% omitted, 5.6% distorted; behaviour deltas (Table 17): critical omission $+18.2$ points repeated work, progress/state loss $+13.8$, constraint/goal distortion $+10.5$ unverified commitment; information recovery attempted in 95.1% of applicable failures.
load_bearing_assumption: That the fall from $\mathrm{pass}^3$ (three full successes, 100% by construction) to 46.0-68.5% strict Avg@3 measures $M_b$ and nothing else: 'The task, boundary environment state, executor, and budget are therefore fixed across compactors, leaving $M_{b}$ as the primary variable' (sec. 2.2); 'Because every reference task was solved in all three original rollouts (pass3), the executor is stable on the uncompressed task, and failures after compaction are unlikely to stem from ordinary rollout variance' (App. F.2). Three things carry it. (i) The uncompressed control is the screening run, not a continuation: no arm continues from the boundary state with the full $H_b$ under the $T - b$ budget, and $T - b$ is the remainder of one chosen successful rollout, not of the other two; the paper's own budget diagnostics show the budget is loose for some (41% of late Coding successes finish within two actions, App. E.4) and binding for others (Case E, $T - b = 3$, Table 23), so part of the gap is budget-times-variance, unmeasured. (ii) That a character ratio equalises the compactors: 86.0% of compactions are within tolerance (Table 9), Workspace 59.7% and Doubao 52.5%, and misses 'are evaluated as returned' (App. B.5); the retained head is outside the ratio ('whose retained system prompt is roughly 30k characters', App. A.2), so the executor's assembled context is not 10% of anything. (iii) That one sample of $M_b$ per instance, at temperature 1.0 or API default (Table 4), stands for the compactor: 'Holding $M_{b}$ fixed isolates downstream rollout variability from variation in compaction generation' (App. A.4); compaction variance is designed out, not measured. If (i)-(iii) fail, the 43.3-point mean loss is an upper bound on what compaction costs, and the model ranking (CIs of ranks 1-2 overlap, Table 12) is noise around a length-and-budget artefact.
weakest_component: The error analysis (RQ4, App. G) that supplies the paper's mechanism claim ('compaction can distort as well as omit task state', sec. 1). (1) Labels come from GPT-5.6-Sol, itself the fourth-ranked compactor under evaluation; human validation is 'We manually reviewed a subset of the annotations against the source trajectories and the rubric' (App. G.2) with no count, no agreement statistic. (2) Statistics are 'computed over failed continuations only' (App. G.1), so no base rate of each error among successful continuations exists; the $+18.2$-point 'repeated work' delta (Table 17) is a within-failure association, and whether premature commitment predicts failure at all is not shown; 'A label does not require a downstream consequence' (App. G.1). (3) Labels are 'potentially overlapping' and 85.8-92.5% of failures carry at least one, so the taxonomy has little discriminating power as used. Next: (4) Workspace is 25 tasks of an internal suite ('CompanyBench serves as an additional validation domain rather than a core public component of the benchmark', sec. 2.1) with CIs such as [4.0, 36.0] and [0.0, 20.0] (Table 12) and no environment-only control (Table 14 covers Coding and Search only). (5) IRC is an intervention no harness runs: 4.6-11.8 compactor calls per instance with 'The full history and incumbent are both supplied' (App. B.2), so the measured object is the model under iterative editing, and the one-shot compaction that the cited harnesses perform (sec. 4) is never scored against it. (6) The executor on Search and Coding is Claude Opus 4.8 and the winning compactor is Claude Opus 5; a family effect is untested (on Workspace, under GPT-5.5 Codex, GPT-5.6-Sol scores 20.0 and Gemini 3.8 Flash 56.0, which cuts against it but on 25 tasks).
regime: Compactors: 12 API models (Table 3), each at its 'strongest available reasoning or thinking configuration' (sec. 3.1): Claude Opus 5 (adaptive, effort max), GPT-5.6-Sol (effort max), Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (thinking high), Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4 Pro, HY3, GLM 5.3 Flash, GLM 5.2, Qwen 3.8 Flash (effort max or high), Qwen 3.7 Plus (thinking budget 65,536), Doubao Seed 2.1 Pro (effort high); temperature 1.0 and top-$p$ 0.9-1.0 or API default, max output 65,536-131,072 tokens (Table 4). Executors: Claude Opus 4.8 (high reasoning effort) with Serper search and Jina page access for BrowseComp and a SWE-bench Verified sandbox for Coding; GPT-5.5 Codex in the native CompanyBench runtime (Table 6, App. F.1). Judges: Gemini 3.5 Flash on Search answers; repository tests on Coding; CompanyBench's own evaluator (Table 6). Tasks: 200 (79 / 96 / 25), filtered to $\mathrm{pass}^3$ and at least eight interaction rounds; reference trajectories average 30.4 / 19.4 / 58.5 rounds and 35.3K / 8.8K / 122.8K tokens (Table 1); one boundary per trajectory, 26 / 26 / 27 Search, 33 / 31 / 32 Coding, 8 / 9 / 8 Workspace at 25 / 50 / 75% (Table 11). Compaction input: 2.3K to 90.0K tokens (Table 11); Case B prefix 703k characters (Table 20). Retention: 10% of body characters, 2,400 compactions, one $M_b$ per instance, three continuations each (App. A.4); other ratios 5-80% run on 100 tasks for length only, no downstream (App. B.6). Horizon: continuation budget $T - b$ from 3 to 140 actions in the cases (Tables 22-23). Accuracy band: 46.0-68.5% overall, 7.4-55.6% late-boundary Search, 81.2-90.6% late-boundary Coding (Table 13). Annotation: GPT-5.6-Sol high effort, 200 inventories of 27.9 units on average (range 17-44) (App. G.1). Cost: tokens, dollars and wall-clock of compaction or continuation unknown (not in text). Code and data release: project website named (compaction-eval.github.io); release status unknown (not in text). arXiv v1, 19 Nov 2026 (Fudan, Tencent Hunyuan, Tsinghua SIGS); venue not stated.
information_asymmetry: The boundary splits information three ways, and the paper's own words set the frame: 'working-context compaction is inherently prospective: what matters is not only what information was important in the past, but what information must be carried forward for future execution' (sec. 4). (A) Compactor vs future. At boundary $b$ the compactor holds $H_b$ and a generic instruction; what the continuation will need exists only in the remainder $(a_{b+1}, \ldots, a_T)$ of the reference run and in the three new continuations. The paper has that remainder for every instance and never uses it as the ruler: the Stage A inventory of 'the information required to continue the task' is written by GPT-5.6-Sol from 'the original task and the complete pre-boundary history $H_{b}$, without access to any compacted context or continuation' (App. G.1), so 'needed' is itself a forward guess by a model, not a hindsight count of which units the successful remainder consumed. Inference: the hindsight ruler (units of $H_b$ the reference remainder or the successful continuations actually touched) exists in the released traces and would give a per-instance oracle retention set and a minimal-$M_b$ length, against which the 10% character budget is arbitrary; the paper's Case E ('the proportion of the history that was load-bearing', Table 23 discussion) gestures at it without computing it. (B) Executor vs compactor. The executor receives $M_b$ as 'Preloaded assistant context' (Table 7), its own prior words, with no mark of which statuses the compactor added; Case C shows a 'gold-rush' framing the source executor introduced in its queries inherited 'as if it were part of the task' and a status for the candidate 'added, not lost' (Table 21 discussion), Case F shows the same fact written as a decision or a question deciding 4 vs 39 actions (Table 24). The paper measures this only by qualitative cases and the within-failure deltas of Table 17; the executor-side quantity (does the executor act differently when a status is flagged as compactor-added vs source-stated) is not measured. (C) Environment vs context. Measured directly and new here: the environment-only arm (Table 14) separates what the repository carries from what $M_b$ carries, giving $M_b$'s incremental value as $-2.7$ / $+14.6$ / $+14.2$ points on Coding and $+26.0$ / $+27.2$ / $+27.2$ on Search, and the edit indicator 86.9 vs 53.0 (App. F.3). What this paper measures at a compaction boundary: one compaction event per trajectory, twelve compactors at a fixed character ratio with IRC editing, the same executor continuing under the reference remainder budget, three continuations per fixed $M_b$, an environment-only control on two of three domains, a stage split, and LLM-labelled errors over failures. What it does not measure, each from the text: no full-$H_b$ continuation from the boundary under $T - b$ (the control is the screening run, App. C.2 and F.2); no repeated compaction of the same run ('each trajectory is assigned to exactly one boundary rather than evaluated at all three', App. C.3), so iterated compaction over a long task is outside the instrument; no second sample of $M_b$ ('Each compacted context is generated once and evaluated with three independent continuations', sec. 3.1), so compactor variance at temperature 1.0 is excluded by design; no token or cost accounting ('Compaction itself is not subtracted from this executor-action budget', App. A.4; the ratio 'is therefore a text-length constraint, not an exact fraction of an executor’s token window or of the full assembled context', App. B.1; mean 4.6-11.8 IRC calls per instance each carrying the full history, Table 9 and App. B.2); no downstream result at any ratio but 10% ('It measures only the realized compaction length; no downstream continuation is run', App. B.6); no one-shot harness compaction scored against the IRC product; no error base rate among successes (App. G.1). Relative to what the pipeline has already found occupied (unsourced entries: SJC; full-history controls and binding loss: ARCBench, handoff audit; re-compaction variance: TRACE and the earlier Compact-Bench, a different artefact from this CompAct-Bench), the open quantity here is (A): a hindsight-defined oracle retention set per boundary, against which both the 10% budget and the compactors' omission and distortion rates could be scored as distance from sufficiency rather than as distance from the whole history. Inference, labelled: the paper's traces make that computable at zero model cost once released.
occupies: Published: a 200-instance compaction benchmark (79 BrowseComp, 96 SWE-bench Verified, 25 internal CompanyBench) built from $\mathrm{pass}^3$ trajectories cut once at 25 / 50 / 75%, with IRC (iterative character-ratio calibration to 10%, tolerance 3%, up to 30 calls), a fixed executor continuing under the reference remainder budget, strict Avg@3 scoring and a 'budget exhaustion' vs 'early failure' split; the result that twelve frontier compactors score 46.0-68.5% (mean 56.7%) with Claude Opus 5 first and Gemini 3.8 Flash second (Table 2); the stage reversal (Search falls 52.9 to 34.6, Coding rises 64.0 to 86.1 across boundaries, Table 13) explained by where state lives, with the environment-only control (Table 14) and the pre-boundary edit indicator (86.9 vs 53.0, App. F.3); the finding that about 92-98% of failures are budget exhaustion and that failed continuations attempt information recovery 95.1% of the time (App. E.4, G.3); the six-label error taxonomy (critical omission, factual distortion, premature commitment, lost resolution, progress/state loss, constraint/goal distortion) with its within-failure behaviour deltas and the headline that 'compaction can distort as well as omit task state' (sec. 1); the calibration result that IRC holds 5-20% targets but realised ratios level off at a few tens of thousands of characters for 40-80% targets (Table 10); and seven annotated cases (A-G) including the same-fact-different-status contrast (Case F) and the located-but-unmaterialised helper (Case G). Not claimed in the text: any training or recipe; a full-history continuation control; repeated compaction; compactor-sample variance; token or dollar cost; results at ratios other than 10%; Workspace without-history control; human agreement numbers for the annotation.

neighbors.title: Slipstream: Trajectory-Grounded Compaction Validation for Long-Horizon Agents
neighbors.trick: Run the compactor asynchronously while the agent keeps acting on the uncompressed context, then have a judge check the candidate summary against those independently generated next steps (forward intent, key facts, constraints), gaining up to 8.8 points of accuracy and 39.7% less latency on SWE-bench Verified and BrowseComp (abstract fetched); cited here only as a setting where compaction 'operates on the interaction history accumulated during an ongoing agent task' (sec. 4), yet it is the one published system that uses the hindsight signal this benchmark leaves on the table: the agent's own continuation as the ruler of what the summary must carry.

neighbors.title: Context Compaction Theory
neighbors.trick: Model compaction as two games (select a subset of state, or generate a bounded message), prove the generation game equals one-way communication complexity so the minimum compaction budget for a query set at a target error is a known quantity, and use it to score Anthropic's compaction endpoint against the optimum on set-membership queries (abstract fetched); cited here among works on deciding 'what information should remain active' (sec. 4); it supplies exactly the sufficiency ruler this paper's fixed 10% character budget lacks, for toy queries rather than agent remainders.

neighbors.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
neighbors.trick: Train the agent with compaction inside the RL loop so the policy learns to act across its own summaries; cited here as evidence that 'Working-context compaction has emerged as a practical mechanism for this purpose' (sec. 4); abstract not fetched (two-neighbour limit); this benchmark would be its natural held-out test and does not report any trained compactor.

theme_fit.why: the lane's object, a compaction summary, costed in downstream task completion at a controlled character ratio with the same executor continuing (100% to 46.0-68.5%, Table 2), with the one genuinely new control in a dense lane: the environment-only arm that prices what the summary carries beyond the repository (Table 14); what it leaves unmeasured (full-history continuation, repeated compaction, compactor variance, tokens, ratios other than 10%, a hindsight sufficiency ruler) is the lane's open list, and the first three of those are already occupied by ARCBench, the handoff audit and TRACE per the W44-W45 kill records

benchmark design with instruments attached: pass^3 screening to separate rollout variance from treatment, a matched remainder budget, task-level stratified bootstrap with shared indices, and an LLM-labelled error taxonomy whose validity (annotator is a compared model; labels over failures only; unquantified human check) is the kind of attribution gap the lane studies

compaction as a serving lever is the stated motivation but no token, latency or dollar cost is measured; IRC spends 4.6-11.8 full-history compactor calls per instance (Table 9) and 'Compaction itself is not subtracted from this executor-action budget' (App. A.4), so the cost side of the trade-off is absent

limitations_as_complaints: My benchmark fixes the summary at one tenth of the history's characters and scores the downstream task only there; when I sweep the ratio from 5% to 80% I measure only how long the summary came out, so I cannot tell anyone how much context a compactor can drop before the executor starts failing: 'This calibration study uses 100 tasks (40 Search, 40 Coding, and 20 Workspace) with the boundary at $50\%$ of the reference trajectory and the same $\epsilon$ and $K$ as the main configuration. It measures only the realized compaction length; no downstream continuation is run' (App. B.6); 'Unless otherwise specified, the main evaluation uses a $10\%$ target retention ratio' (sec. 2.2).

My compaction score is defined only on tasks my executor already solves three times out of three, each cut exactly once, so I cannot say what compaction costs on the long tasks that actually hit the context limit, nor what the second and third compaction of the same run do: 'This construction conditions the benchmark on tasks the executor can solve without compaction. It therefore measures robustness of a successful execution to replacing accumulated history with $M_{b}$, not unconstrained task-solving ability' (App. C.2); 'To control cost, each trajectory is assigned to exactly one boundary rather than evaluated at all three' (App. C.3).

I compare compactors at a matched character count but never count what the compaction itself cost: my calibration makes up to thirty model calls per instance with the whole history in each, I charge none of it to the budget, and my ratio is characters of body text, not the executor's tokens or its assembled context, so I cannot state the price of the summary in the currency anyone pays: 'Compaction itself is not subtracted from this executor-action budget' (App. A.4); '$r$ is therefore a text-length constraint, not an exact fraction of an executor’s token window or of the full assembled context' (App. B.1); 'whose retained system prompt is roughly 30k characters: at a $10\%$ body-retention target, the executor’s assembled context is therefore considerably longer than $M_{b}$ alone' (App. A.2).
